full_judgment:
4. Mr. Kazi Abdul Gofran, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that the petitioner is not a business or a trading concern in Bangladesh. They have, under the convention Annexure B and the permission Annexure A, set up a liaison office in Dhaka with the purpose and intent as provided for in Annexure A to this petition. They have no income here in this country and the expenditures are met from the remittances received from abroad. It is submitted that when the petitioner has no income and when they are maintaining them from foreign remittances they have been protected under Annexures A and B and there can be no assessment on their supposed incomes. It is submitted that the convention was entered into for avoiding double taxation. Mr. Kazi Abdul Gofran submitted that the materials on record indicate that the petitioner is supplying only data and information’s to their principal office in Seoul, Korea. They have not entered into any agreement with any party here in Bangladesh nor they opened LC for importing goods and selling those in the market. It is submitted that this convention was made under the provision of section 144 of Income Tax Act, 1984 and this has the backing of the law. The learned Advocate leading us through the initial assessment order made by the Deputy Commissioner and also the judgment passed by the Appellate Joint Commissioner of Taxes and the Tribunal submitted that there is absolutely no material to hold that the petitioner themselves did any business in Bangladesh. It appears that the taxes has been assessed only on the ground that the principal office of the petitioner in Seoul, Korea have exported certain goods to Bangladesh and that is the reason behind the assessment of taxes. Nowhere it was found that this petitioner was doing any business in Bangladesh. 

 8. We have gone through the assessment order, judgment of the Appellate Joint Commissioner of Taxes as well as the judgment of the Tribunal and also gone through the permission and the provision of the convention. There is absolutely nothing to show that the petitioner has a permanent establishment in Bangladesh and that they were actually doing business here in this country and that they themselves sold their products to any person in Bangladesh. If any profit is earned by the petitioners’ principal office in Korea under the convention they will be taxed in Korea. But they cannot be taxed for their earnings in Korea in Bangladesh which is protected under the convention which is a solemn document entered into between these two Governments and which has the backing of section 144 of the Income Tax Act, 1984.
